title: Smoked Haddock Chowder
subtitle: Milky, leek-based fish chowder with sweet potato
excerpt: A thick, hearty chowder of smoked haddock with leek, potato, and sweetcorn in a creamy broth. Quick to make, deeply comforting, and one of the best things to do with smoked haddock.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chowder is an American and British coastal tradition of thick soup made with fish or shellfish, potato, and dairy. The New England clam chowder is the best-known version, but smoked fish chowders are a strong tradition on both sides of the Atlantic. The British version using smoked haddock, leek, and potato is a natural combination given the availability of smoked haddock in Scottish and northern English fishing communities.

content.text: Do not let the chowder boil once the cream and fish go in. Boiling splits the cream and makes the fish rubbery. Once the fish is in the pot, keep the heat at the lowest simmer you can manage. Use undyed smoked haddock if possible; the dyed version will turn the broth an unpleasant yellow. Serve with crusty bread.

items.preparation: skin removed, cut into large chunks

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the leek for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the milk, stirring to prevent lumps. Add the fish stock and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer, add the potato, and cook for 12 minutes until the potato is tender.
Reduce the heat to very low. Add the cream, sweetcorn, and smoked haddock chunks. Cook for 5 minutes without boiling until the fish is just cooked through and flaking. Remove the bay leaves.
Taste for salt and pepper. The haddock will have seasoned the broth significantly. Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.
